issues.legal_issue: Eligibility for benefits under a scheme depends on satisfying its cumulative land-purchase and possession requirements.
material_facts: A housing cooperative sought benefits under a scheme that required a society to have purchased the land before a specified planning declaration and to hand over vacant and peaceful possession when entering an advance agreement.

The Court found that the cooperative had not fulfilled the prior-purchase condition; it was not the owner or in possession of the land and could not hand over vacant and peaceful possession as required.
The cooperative appealed the judgments upholding the denial of benefits.
issues.conclusion: The cooperative was not entitled to the scheme’s benefits because it did not satisfy the required conditions.
issues.legal_principle: The scheme’s first clause imposed cumulative requirements: the society had to be registered as required by law and had to purchase the land before publication of the relevant declaration under Section 50(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Tatha Gram Nivesh Adhiniyam, 1973. Clause 3 separately made handover of vacant and peaceful possession to the Authority at the time of an advance agreement mandatory for availing the benefit. An advance agreement could be entered into, but it did not dispense with the possession requirement.

rule.if: benefit_denial_appeal and scheme_requires_prior_land_purchase and claimant_did_not_purchase_land_before_declaration and scheme_requires_vacant_possession_handover and claimant_cannot_handover_vacant_possession

predicates.benefit_denial_appeal: A claimant appeals a decision upholding the denial of benefits under a scheme.
predicates.scheme_requires_prior_land_purchase: The scheme requires the claimant to purchase the relevant land before a specified declaration.
predicates.claimant_did_not_purchase_land_before_de: The claimant did not purchase the relevant land before the specified declaration.
predicates.scheme_requires_vacant_possession_handov: The scheme requires the claimant to hand over vacant and peaceful possession of the relevant land when entering an advance agreement.
predicates.claimant_cannot_handover_vacant_possessi: The claimant is not in a position to hand over vacant and peaceful possession of the relevant land as required.

issues.definition: When a claimant appealing denial of scheme benefits has not met the scheme’s prior-purchase and vacant-possession requirements, the claimant is not entitled to those benefits.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain equal treatment by relying on benefits wrongly granted to other ineligible applicants.
material_facts: The claimant argued that other societies in a similar position had received the scheme’s benefits.
The Authority disputed that assertion, but the Court considered the argument on the assumption that benefits had been granted to ineligible societies.
issues.conclusion: Even if other ineligible societies received the benefits, that did not give the claimant a right to them or establish discrimination.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require repetition of an unlawful action to achieve equal treatment; equal treatment presupposes a similar legal footing and does not recognize negative equality. The Court relied on Union of India v. International Trading Co. (2003) 5 SCC 437.

predicates.benefit_denial_appeal: A claimant appeals a decision upholding the denial of benefits under a scheme.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_other_grants: The claimant relies on benefits granted to other applicants as a basis for demanding the same treatment.
predicates.other_grants_were_to_ineligible_applican: The other applicants who received benefits did not qualify for them.

issues.definition: When a claimant appealing a denial relies on benefits wrongly granted to ineligible applicants, those grants do not create an entitlement to equal treatment.
